headline: A preprint proposes context-conditioned control of multi-token decoding horizons
summary: A new preprint proposes choosing the number of draft tokens in multi-token speculative decoding from context-dependent acceptance forecasts and measured round costs. Its controller selects the horizon before drafting, uses exact-verifier feedback to update online, and is paired with a regret analysis. In five draft-target pairings over AIME 2025 and GSM8K, the authors report small, uneven gains over fixed horizons (up to 10%, with 8 of 10 settings matching or ahead). The larger up-to-4.1x figure is against plain decoding. The tests disable the KV-cache and use no fixed random seed; one AIME table row has an unexplained 3.7x adaptive/fixed throughput gap. These are credible but unconfirmed paper-reported results, not an established serving improvement.
